name: Link card
purpose: Makes one destination stand out, on a card of its own that's a link, with its name large and bold, such as the user's council on Home. A description above the name can say what it's for.

origin.notes: The app's StoredLocalAuthorityCardView, which Home's Your local services draws for the user's council, or a card for each of two: a card in fills.surfaceList, its corners rounded 10pt, with a solid shadow 3pt below it in strokes.cardDefault, padded 16pt. Its name is Title 2 Bold in text.link, after its description, if it has one, in Body, text.secondary. Nothing in it is about councils, so it's here as a card for any one link.

href.description: Where the card goes, such as the council's website.

description.description: Shown above the name, in grey, saying what it's for, such as County councils are usually responsible for services like education, social care and transport.

inputs.content: The name of where it goes, as text, such as Central Bedfordshire Council.

events.name: click
events.description: From the link it draws, when it's pressed, before it goes to its href.

rules: Use it for one destination worth making stand out, such as the user's own council. For a list of links, use a grouped list.
Put it under a section heading saying what it is, such as Your local services.
Keep the name to what the user will recognise, such as the council's own name.
Give each card a description when there are two or more, saying how they differ, as the app does for a county council and a district council.

avoid.when: For a link within a line of text
For a screen in the app, among others

references.description: Your local services, with the user's council, in light mode
Two councils, each card with a description, in light mode

examples.name: With a description
examples.html: <govuk-app-link-card href="https://www.derbyshire.gov.uk" description="County councils are usually responsible for services like education, social care and transport">Derbyshire County Council</govuk-app-link-card>
